paragraphs: R. Yishmael ben Pabi, High Priest and a pious man. When he died, the splendor of the priesthood ceased (chapter Eglah Arufah, mishnah 15). But his household members were men of force [the printed wording בנו ביתו is difficult] (Rashi), end of chapter Makom SheNahagu (57a). A heavenly voice went forth concerning him in the Temple courtyard: 'Let Yishmael, Pinḥas's student, enter.' He served as High Priest for ten years and prepared one [red] heifer (Parah, chapter 3). In Seder HaDorot, under R. Yehoshua ben Ḥananyah, Yuḥasin writes in Josippon's name that he served only one year and prepared the last heifer [כרה as printed; provisional reading]; end [of quotation]. In his days were Ḥanamel the Egyptian and Eini ben HaKof (see his entry), in Hillel's days. His mother made him a tunic worth a hundred maneh; he performed an individual service in it and handed it over to the public, Yoma (35b). In Tosefta, Parah, chapter 2: R. Yishmael says, 'Ben Pabi instructed that one [heifer] be prepared with a person who had immersed that day'. It appears to be a scribal error.
